name: R:BASE
tagline: Windows desktop relational database and 4GL app builder, sold continuously since the 1980s; now at R:BASE 11.
description: R:BASE is a relational database and rapid application development environment for Windows, created by Wayne Erickson in 1981 and first sold by Microrim as R:BASE 4000 for MS-DOS in 1983. In the 1980s it was the main rival to dBASE; since 1998 it has been owned by R:BASE Technologies of Murrysville, Pennsylvania, which still ships regular builds. A single package bundles the database engine, SQL, a 4GL programming language, form, report and label designers, multi-user file sharing and ODBC connectivity, plus a family of companion utilities. R:BASE 11 Update 3 shipped in June 2026, and an AI assistant for plain-English queries was added in September 2026. It suits small businesses and long-lived line-of-business apps that already run on it.

pricing.notes: Sold per license with update/support plans; a 30-day trial is available.

scale.notes: File-sharing multi-user database on a Windows network share; sized for departmental applications.

strengths: All-in-one: database, SQL, 4GL, forms and reports in one Windows package
More than four decades of backward-compatible applications
Still actively maintained with frequent update builds
Low barrier for small businesses building line-of-business apps
weaknesses: Small, ageing ecosystem and developer pool
Not suited to web-scale, cloud-native or high-concurrency use
useCases: Desktop data entry and reporting tools
